title: What Is a Founder Identity?
hook: Not every entrepreneur is built the same - and that actually matters.
seo_keywords: founder identity, income path for beginners
script_line1: People say 'start a business' like it's one thing. But a person who's great with their hands and wants to do service work is a completely different type of entrepreneur than someone who wants to build digital products or do remote consulting.
script_line2: If you try to build the wrong type of business for how you actually work - how you think, what you're good at, what you want your day to look like - it's going to be a grind in a bad way.
script_line3: Founder Identity is the idea that you have a type. A pattern. A set of traits that point toward certain income paths and away from others.
script_line4: The Income Spectrum app has a quiz that helps you identify yours. It asks about how you work, what kind of value you create, how you want to operate.
script_line5: From that it gives you a Founder File - a profile of your founder type - with income paths and resources that fit it. It's not a personality test for fun. It's meant to save you time.
overlay_1: Your founder type shapes which income paths fit you
overlay_2: Not every business model fits every person
cta: Take the Founder Identity Quiz in the app at incomespectrum.app - it's free and it's genuinely useful.

title: What the Quiz Actually Tells You
hook: It's not asking you how motivated you are - it goes deeper than that.
seo_keywords: founder identity, income path for beginners, business platforms for independent workers
script_line1: The Founder Identity Quiz is not one of those fluffy 'what kind of entrepreneur are you' quizzes where you answer five questions and get told you're a visionary.
script_line2: It's trying to figure out how you work. What kind of value you naturally create. Whether you're better suited for service-based income, product-based income, digital work, hands-on work, consulting.
script_line3: Once it has a picture of that, it gives you your Founder File. And the Founder File doesn't just give you a label - it points you toward income platforms that match your type and certifications that might be relevant.
script_line4: Instead of just browsing the entire site hoping something clicks, you start with a clearer sense of direction. Here's your type, here's where to look first.
script_line5: Takes about five minutes. If you've been feeling scattered about where to focus your energy, it's worth doing just to get some clarity.
overlay_1: The quiz maps HOW you work - not just what you want
overlay_2: Your Founder File = your personalized resource map
cta: Go to incomespectrum.app and take the quiz - it'll make the rest of the site make more sense.

title: The Different Founder Types
hook: There are a few main categories - and most people fall somewhere specific.
seo_keywords: founder identity, income options for entrepreneurs, how to start earning independently
script_line1: When you take the Founder Identity Quiz, the result places you into a founder type. Here's a rough overview.
script_line2: Hands-on founders - physical, skilled, or trade-based work. Contractors, service providers, technicians. They tend to do well on Angi Pro, Thumbtack, or platforms built for local service work.
script_line3: Digital founders - more online, content or product-based or remote service work. Fiverr, Clarity, Catalant, Outschool fit differently here.
script_line4: Service-role founders - professional services like bookkeeping, consulting, coaching. NACPB, AIPB, Clarity fit this lane.
script_line5: And there are hybrid types - people who cross multiple categories. The quiz figures out where you land and your Founder File tells you what to do with that information.
overlay_1: Hands-on / Digital / Service / Product - which are you?
overlay_2: Your type = your income path filter
cta: Take the Founder Identity Quiz at incomespectrum.app to find out which type fits you.

title: How to Use Your Founder Type to Pick the Right Income Path
hook: Knowing your founder type without doing anything with it is kind of useless.
seo_keywords: founder identity, income options for entrepreneurs, business platforms for independent workers
script_line1: So let's say you take the quiz and you're a hands-on service founder. Now what?
script_line2: The practical move is to filter the Income Options section through that. Instead of looking at every platform, you already know - hands-on service founders should be looking at Angi Pro, Thumbtack, maybe RealPage or MyVendorCenter depending on your work.
script_line3: Then look at Education and Training for certifications that strengthen your credibility. If it's trades, look at skilled trades credentials.
script_line4: Then check your state's page - because licensing matters for service work and every state is different.
script_line5: That's the flow. Quiz, Founder File, filtered platform list, certifications, state resources. Designed to work in order.

overlay_2: Stop browsing everything - start with your type

title: Why Most People Skip This Step and Struggle
hook: I see this constantly - people jump straight to platforms before they know what fits them.
seo_keywords: founder identity, income path for beginners, how to start earning independently
script_line1: Someone decides they want to start earning on their own. First instinct - find a platform, sign up, start. And that makes sense. The impulse is good.
script_line2: But what happens is they end up on a platform that doesn't match how they work or what they're good at. They spend weeks trying to get traction. Nothing clicks.
script_line3: They think they're doing something wrong or they're not cut out for this. But really they just picked the wrong lane.
script_line4: The Founder Identity Quiz exists to help you skip that mismatch. A short investment of time upfront that helps you aim better.
script_line5: It doesn't tell you what to do. It tells you what type of work you're actually built for, and then points you toward platforms and resources that fit that type.
